_comment: The destination field map. This file is the single source for which image field
becomes which SQL column, and the writer builds its MERGE statements from it at
runtime. Transcribed from docs/lld/00-foundations.md sections 4.3, 4.4 and 4.5.
Offsets are NOT declared: rule R2 makes the image packed in declared order with
no padding, so an offset is the running sum of the widths before it. Declaring
them too would be a second source of truth for the same arithmetic.
Bit indices ARE declared, and must equal the column's index. They are redundant
on purpose: a reordered column list with stale bits fails the load instead of
silently re-mapping every live entry and stored digest.
imageLen is declared and checked against the computed sum, so a width typo is
caught here rather than becoming a quiet layout change.
Widths are WIRE widths (R1). The image holds exactly what the exchange sent,
big-endian and unscaled; scale, epoch and blank-trim conversions happen in the

destinations.name: MD_TOKEN_QUOTE
destinations._contributors: 7200 and 7208 are mutually exclusive and the choice is the exchange's, without notice (bible 4.8a), so both are declared. A build that knows only one goes blind the day it switches.

columns._note: MBP_INFORMATION[10]: 10 records of 12 bytes. Five best buys then five best sells, copied as one run. BbBuySellFlag is discarded because the side is positional. Prices inside the run are scaled.
BCAST_HEADER.LogTime, not TimeStamp2 -- which is the machine number, not a time.

destinations.name: MD_SECURITY_MASTER
destinations._contributors: 7340 is the periodic re-send of 7305, identical structure.

columns._note: Fixed width, blank-padded. lenBit -1 means the length is implicit and the writer right-trims at bind time; there is no NUL terminator (bible 2.6).

destinations.name: MD_MARKET_STATUS
destinations._contributors: Five contributors, which is why MaxContributors must exceed the HLD's four. They share one row per market_type and differ only in which last wrote it, so transcode (bit 0) is how a reader tells Open from Closed.

columns._note: Length comes from message_len (bit 1), a different image field. The wire carries 239 bytes but the bible says the tail past the valid length is not meaningful; 128 is a schema choice, not a limit imageSize forces. The region is fully rewritten and zero-filled past the valid length (R5), which is what the digest depends on.
